Title: Denial of Service via X.509 name constraint parsing containing extremely long GEN_DIRNAME (CVE-2024-6119)
Analysis: Under CVE-2024-6119, the function `X509_NAME_oneline()` does not properly handle extremely long or specially structured custom directory names (GEN_DIRNAME) within certificate extensions or subject/issuer names. Specifically, inside `i2v_GENERAL_NAME` (defined in `crypto/x509/v3_san.c`), when formatting `GEN_DIRNAME` via `X509_NAME_oneline()`, a fixed-size buffer `oline[256]` is used. When a carefully crafted malicious certificate containing a subject/issuer name or subject alternative name (SAN) directory name field longer than 255 characters is parsed, `X509_NAME_oneline()` attempts to write to this buffer, but since it is called with `len = sizeof(oline)` (which is 256), the return string might either get truncated or, under certain internal allocations/EBCDIC conversions, cause unexpected memory constraints. Specifically, in previous versions or configurations, `X509_NAME_oneline` can also return NULL or fail, or cause a null-pointer dereference/undefined behavior when the caller does not check for NULL or handles buffer boundaries unsafely. An attacker can construct a certificate with a large/deep directory name (GEN_DIRNAME) SAN extension that triggers a crash (Denial of Service) when parsed or printed via APIs like SSL_CTX_set_verify, CMP validation, or other diagnostic prints that utilize `X509_NAME_oneline()` or generalize directory name prints.
